evidence.observation: The dependency path is checkout-web -> payment-api -> auth-gateway; AUTH-2026-0318 changed auth-gateway issuer and JWKS cache settings at 14:05Z.

At 14:10Z, checkout-web had an 18.7% HTTP 401 rate and 2400 ms p95, payment-api had a 21.2% HTTP 401 rate with notes citing an invalid issuer, and auth-gateway had a 28.4% HTTP 401 rate with issuer mismatch.

After deployment of AUTH-2026-0318, auth-gateway used partner-v2 but allowed_issuers remained partner-v1; validation failed with issuer_not_allowed. The log names restoring partner-v2 or reverting the change as rollback candidates.
payment-api rejected the request after auth-gateway returned issuer_not_allowed/invalid_issuer.
checkout-web submit_order failed with status 401 from payment-api, and the user checkout flow remained blocked while static assets recovered.

excluded_red_herrings.why_not_primary: Query p95 was 35 ms with zero errors, and no failing checkout transaction reached orders-db.
The errors were isolated to images; static assets served normally after retry, while checkout submits still failed on payment authentication.
These are downstream effects of repeated authentication rejection, not evidence of a database or frontend availability cause.

recommended_next_steps: Immediately roll back AUTH-2026-0318 or correct auth-gateway allowed_issuers to include partner-v2, following change control.
Refresh or invalidate the affected JWKS cache namespace and confirm partner-v2 keys and issuer configuration agree.
Verify a partner-token validation succeeds at auth-gateway, then a create_payment request succeeds at payment-api, then an end-to-end checkout submit succeeds at checkout-web.
Monitor HTTP 401/5xx rates and p95 latency for checkout-web, payment-api, and auth-gateway; confirm no new issuer mismatch events.
